name: Rose Fong
equipment: A green wool coat and a cardigan (no armor)
.32 pocket pistol, her father's, which he insists she carry walking home from the swing shift, 8 rounds loaded, in her bag
Operator's headset (hers, she bought it) and her badge from the Chinatown Telephone Exchange
A small black notebook with every unusual thing she has seen on Washington Street since 1936, with times
The ledger for her uncle's print shop on Jackson Street, which she keeps on Sundays
A night-school textbook: Elements of Newspaper Reporting
features: Knows the Block (City-Born origin, San Francisco: advantage on Streetwise checks to find a person, place or service in the city)

Press Pass (stringer's card from a Chinese-language daily on Grant Avenue: she gets into press rooms and courtrooms; a source never gets burned; advantage on Persuasion to get someone to talk off the record)
The Morgue (Research takes half the time; once per long rest, one fact the paper has printed about a named person, business or address, no roll)
Ink by the Barrel (Intimidation with INT and advantage when she threatens to print; the wrong man raises Heat by 1)
Beat: Crime Desk (proficiency in Forensics; she knows which cop at Central Station will talk to the papers)
Follow the Money (Bookkeeper background: she can read a ledger, a bank book or a bill of lading and say where the money went)

personality.traits: I talk fast, write faster and interrupt people when they are being slow. I am funny and I know it. I hate being underestimated, which happens about forty times a day.
personality.ideals: Everybody in this city has a story, including the people the English-language papers never ask. Somebody ought to write theirs down too.
personality.bonds: My uncle Fong Wah, who runs the print shop on Jackson Street and took me in when my parents went back to Taishan, and the twenty women on the switchboard at the exchange, who know more about this neighbourhood than the police ever will.
personality.flaws: I want a byline so badly I will take risks for it I would never let my little cousins take, and I do not tell my uncle where I am going.

appearance: Twenty-four, small and quick, with bobbed black hair, horn-rimmed glasses she pushes up her nose when she is thinking, a green coat, a cardigan with a pencil through the buttonhole, and sensible shoes for running for the cable car.
backstory: Rose Fong was born on Stockton Street in 1914, went to the Commodore Stockton School and Galileo High, and has worked the switchboard at the Chinatown Telephone Exchange since she was eighteen, connecting two thousand subscribers by name in English, Cantonese and Taishanese. She strings for a Chinese-language daily on Grant Avenue, takes a night-school journalism course on Tuesdays, and has sent eleven stories to English-language papers on Market Street, all of which came back. On the night of 3 November she heard the shots from the corner of Washington and Kearny and saw a woman in a pale fur hurrying up toward California Street, and wrote it down, and waited for the police to ask. They did not.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Rose is a witness in bc-scenario-001 and a companion from then on, if the party treats her as a colleague. She is the party's window into a neighbourhood the police never canvassed, and she should be the person who knows things because she listens: who was on the street, who rang whom, who has been asking. Make her useful for Research, Investigation and Society, and for knowing where everyone in Chinatown and Jackson Square was at any hour. She is not a guide to anything exotic; she is a sharp young San Franciscan who happens to live four blocks from a murder.
dmNotes.voice: Fast, wry, American, with the switchboard habit of repeating names to fix them ("Mrs. Strand. Strand. Got it."). Says "honestly" a lot. Drops into Cantonese with her uncle and her colleagues without thinking. When she is excited she talks in headlines: "WIDOW IN FUR SEEN ON KEARNY. No? Too much?"
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: be taken seriously, and get a story into an English-language paper under her own name. Secondary: see that the person who killed a man on her street pays for it, because the police did not even ask. Tertiary: protect her uncle and the exchange operators from any trouble she brings home.
dmNotes.secrets: She knows, from the exchange, that a call was put through on Friday morning from a Grant Avenue grocer to the Hotel Grant for "Miss Lind, the foreign lady who buys oranges"; operators are not supposed to listen, and she would lose her job if anyone knew she remembers. She also saw Sergeant Kerrigan in a green Plymouth on Jackson Street at midnight on Thursday, talking to a man from the waterfront, and did not know what it meant.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: guarded until someone asks her a real question and writes down the answer, then fiercely loyal. She gets on best with Kit Vandermeer (rivals first, then friends) and Cass Delaney, whom she admires. Toward Dolan: furious that nobody canvassed her street, until he apologises, which he does in bc-scenario-003 if the party tells him. Toward Magda Ehrlich: immediate sympathy; she knows what it is to have papers people look at twice.
